This endpoint is publicly accessible, serving as the entry point for guest users. Guest sessions provide limited functionality for application exploration before registration.

operations.description:
Register a new member account in the todo app system.

This operation creates a new authenticated user who can create, view, update, and delete their own personal todo items. The member account is created with email and password credentials, with the password being securely hashed before storage in the todo_app_members table.

Upon successful registration, the system automatically issues initial JWT access and refresh tokens, creating a session record in the todo_app_member_sessions table. The member receives immediate authentication credentials allowing them to start using the todo functionality without requiring a separate login step.

The email address must be unique across all members in the system. If the email is already registered, the operation fails with a conflict error. The member kind provides full access to personal todo management features while maintaining data isolation from other members.

Related operations include login for existing members, refresh for token renewal, and logout for session termination. Email verification can be requested separately after registration to confirm the email address ownership.

operations.specification: Implementation: 1) Validate email uniqueness against todo_app_members table 2) Hash password using bcrypt with salt rounds 3) Create member record with email, password_hash 4) Generate JWT access token (short-lived) and refresh token (long-lived) 5) Create session record in todo_app_member_sessions with refresh token hash, expires_at 6) Return member data with tokens. Validation: email format, password minimum 8 characters with complexity requirements. Security: password never returned in response.

operations.description:
Authenticate an existing member and issue access tokens.

This operation validates member credentials (email and password) against the stored password_hash in the todo_app_members table. Upon successful authentication, new JWT access and refresh tokens are generated and returned to the member.

The login operation creates a new session record in the todo_app_member_sessions table containing the refresh token hash and expiration timestamp. This enables secure token refresh without requiring repeated password entry. Members can have multiple active sessions across different devices.

If the provided credentials are invalid, the operation returns an authentication error without distinguishing between non-existent email and incorrect password to prevent email enumeration attacks. The member must have an active account status to successfully authenticate.

This operation is the primary entry point for members returning to the application after their access token has expired or been cleared. Members with valid refresh tokens can alternatively use the refresh endpoint to obtain new access tokens without providing credentials again.
operations.name: login
operations.specification: Implementation: 1) Find member by email in todo_app_members table 2) Verify password against password_hash using bcrypt 3) Check account status is active 4) Generate JWT access token (15 min expiry) and refresh token (7 day expiry) 5) Create session record with refresh_token_hash, member_id, expires_at 6) Return member with tokens. Security: constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks, rate limiting on endpoint.

operations.description:
Refresh member access tokens using a valid refresh token.

This operation extends an authenticated session by issuing new access and refresh tokens without requiring the member to re-enter their password. The provided refresh token is validated against the todo_app_member_sessions table to ensure it exists, belongs to an active member, and has not expired.

Upon successful validation, the system generates new token pairs and updates the session record with the new refresh token hash. The old refresh token is effectively invalidated as only the latest token hash is stored per session. This rotation mechanism enhances security by limiting the window of opportunity for token theft.

Members use this endpoint when their access token expires (typically every 15 minutes) to maintain continuous authentication. The refresh token has a longer lifespan (typically 7 days) but must be used before expiration to prevent forced re-authentication.

If the refresh token is invalid, expired, or the associated member account has been deactivated, the operation fails and the member must log in again with credentials. This operation is essential for maintaining long-lived sessions while adhering to security best practices for token-based authentication.
operations.name: refresh
operations.specification: Implementation: 1) Hash provided refresh token 2) Find matching session in todo_app_member_sessions by refresh_token_hash 3) Verify session not expired (expires_at > now) 4) Verify member account is active 5) Generate new access and refresh tokens 6) Update session with new refresh_token_hash and new expires_at 7) Return member with new tokens. Security: token rotation prevents replay attacks.

operations.name: logout
operations.specification: Extract the Bearer access token from the Authorization header. Validate the JWT token signature, expiration, and blacklist status. Extract the user ID from the token subject claim. Parse the request body to determine logout scope ('current' or 'all'). If scope is 'current': find and revoke the refresh token associated with the current session in todo_app_member_sessions table. If scope is 'all': revoke ALL refresh tokens for the user. Add the access token to the blacklist with its expiration timestamp. Log the logout event to todo_app_audit_logs with user ID, IP address, user agent, and scope. Return success response with logout confirmation details.
operations.description:
Log out an authenticated member and invalidate their session tokens.

This operation allows authenticated members to logout from the Todo application, providing control over session invalidation. Members can choose to logout from just the current session (single device) or from all active sessions across all devices. The operation validates the JWT access token from the Authorization header, identifies the authenticated user, and performs the appropriate token revocation based on the requested scope.

When logging out from the current session only, the system revokes the specific refresh token associated with the current session while preserving other active sessions. When logging out from all sessions, the system revokes all refresh tokens for the user, forcing re-authentication on all devices. In both cases, the current access token is added to a short-term blacklist to prevent its reuse until natural expiration.

Security considerations include proper token validation, comprehensive audit logging of logout events, and consistent error handling. The operation returns a generic success response regardless of the actual logout scope to prevent information leakage. Related operations include the login endpoint (POST /auth/members/login) which creates sessions, and the token refresh endpoint for obtaining new access tokens.

requestBody.description: Logout scope specification determining whether to logout from current session only or all active sessions

responseBody.description: Logout confirmation with details about the invalidated sessions

The member_id is extracted from the JWT authentication token's subject claim. Query the database for the member record matching the authenticated user ID and return the complete member entity including id, email, name, created_at, and updated_at fields. operations.description:
Retrieve the currently authenticated member's complete profile information.

This operation allows authenticated members to view their own account details including their unique identifier, email address, display name, and account timestamps. The member identity is automatically determined from the JWT authentication token provided in the request headers, eliminating the need for explicit path parameters.

Security: This endpoint requires a valid JWT token. Members can only access their own profile information - the system validates that the requesting token matches the returned member record. This ensures strict data isolation between users.

Data returned includes the member's unique UUID identifier, registered email address, display name, account creation timestamp, and last update timestamp. The password_hash field is never exposed in API responses for security reasons.

This operation is typically used when members first access the application or navigate to their account settings page. Related operations include member account updates and password changes.

operations.description:
Update an existing member's account information including personal details, email address, or password.

This operation allows authenticated members to modify their account information stored in the todo_app_members table. The member's identity is verified through their authentication token, and they can only update their own account unless they have administrative privileges.

The operation supports updating:
- Personal information such as name
- Email address (requires re-verification)
- Password (requires current password verification)

When an email address is changed, the system automatically resets the email_verified_at field and sends a new verification email to ensure account security. Password updates require proper hashing and validation of the current password.

Security considerations:
- Only authenticated members can update accounts
- Members can only update their own account unless explicitly authorized as admin
- Email changes trigger re-verification workflow
- Password updates follow security best practices with hashing
- Rate limiting applies to update operations

Related operations:
- GET /members/{memberId} - Retrieve member details
- DELETE /members/{memberId} - Delete member account
- POST /members - Create new member account

If email is being changed, validate format, check uniqueness against other members, reset email_verified_at to null, and queue a verification email. If password is being updated, verify current password, apply bcrypt hashing, and update the password field. Update the name field directly if provided. Return the complete updated member entity with all fields. Handle concurrent modification scenarios with optimistic locking patterns.

operations.name: erase
operations.description:
Permanently delete a member account from the Todo App system.

This operation removes a member record entirely from the todo_app_members table. It is intended for administrative use cases where a member account needs to be completely removed from the system, such as when a user requests account deletion or when terminating accounts that violate terms of service.

When executed, this operation performs a hard delete of the member record identified by the memberId path parameter. All associated data owned by this member, including their todos and session records, will be cascade deleted according to the database foreign key constraints. This action is irreversible and the member data cannot be recovered after deletion.

The operation requires appropriate administrative authorization to prevent unauthorized account deletion. Regular members cannot delete other members' accounts through this endpoint.

Cascade delete all related records: todos owned by this member (todo_app_todos with member_id foreign key), active sessions (todo_app_member_sessions), email verification tokens (todo_app_member_email_verifications), and password reset tokens (todo_app_member_password_resets). Return the deleted member entity for confirmation. Handle case where member does not exist by throwing NotFoundException.

If valid, retrieve the associated member from todo_app_members table and return minimal member information (id and email). If token is invalid or expired, return 401 Unauthorized or 410 Gone respectively. Clean up expired tokens during validation as a maintenance operation.
operations.description:
Verify a password reset token to confirm its validity before allowing password reset.

This operation validates the password reset token that was sent to the member's email address. When a member clicks the password reset link in their email, the application extracts the token and sends it to this endpoint for verification. The endpoint checks the todo_app_password_reset_tokens table to ensure the token exists and has not expired.

Upon successful verification, the endpoint returns minimal member information including the member's ID and email address. This information is required for the subsequent password reset operation where the new password will be set. The member identification ensures that the password change is applied to the correct account.

Security considerations include automatic cleanup of expired tokens during the validation process. Invalid or expired tokens result in appropriate error responses (401 for invalid tokens, 410 for expired tokens) to prevent brute force attempts. The endpoint does not reveal whether an email exists in the system for security reasons.

This verification step is a prerequisite for the actual password reset operation (typically PUT /auth/members/password/reset). The returned member information should be used to construct the subsequent reset request.

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of todo items belonging to the authenticated member.

This operation queries the todo_app_todos table and provides comprehensive search capabilities for members to find and organize their personal tasks. Members can filter todos by status (pending or completed), due date ranges, and perform text searches across titles and descriptions. The operation automatically restricts results to only the authenticated member's todos, ensuring complete data isolation between users.

Pagination is supported with configurable page sizes and sorting options including due date, creation date, status, and title. This enables efficient browsing of large todo lists with optimal performance.

Security considerations: This endpoint requires member authentication. The member_id filter is automatically applied based on the JWT token, ensuring users cannot access other members' todo items. Rate limiting may be applied to prevent abuse of search functionality.

Retrieve detailed information about a specific todo item by its unique identifier.

This operation fetches a single todo from the todo_app_todos table, returning complete details including the title, description, completion status, due date, priority level, and timestamps. The operation enforces ownership validation - only the member who created the todo can retrieve its details.

Security considerations: This endpoint requires member authentication. The system validates that the requesting member is the owner of the specified todo item. If the todo does not exist or does not belong to the authenticated member, a 404 Not Found response is returned to prevent information leakage about other users' todos.

This operation is typically used when a user clicks on a todo item to view its full details or when navigating to an edit page. The response provides all necessary information for displaying the todo in a detail view or populating an edit form.

Required fields include title (non-empty string up to 200 characters). Optional fields include description (detailed task notes up to 2000 characters), priority level (low, medium, high), and due date (ISO 8601 datetime).

Upon successful creation, the todo is assigned a unique UUID identifier, default status of 'pending', and timestamps for creation and last update. The todo is immediately associated with the authenticated member and becomes available for retrieval and management through other API operations.

Health check endpoint for service availability monitoring and load balancer health probes.

The response includes a simple status indicator and timestamp. This endpoint executes quickly and is optimized for frequent polling by health check probes. It should not be used for detailed system diagnostics or business logic validation.

Typical consumers include Kubernetes liveness/readiness probes, AWS ELB health checks, and uptime monitoring services.

The member identity is extracted from the JWT token in the Authorization header, not from this request body. Upon successful logout, the system revokes the appropriate refresh token(s), adds the current access token to a blacklist, and logs the event to todo_app_audit_logs.

ITodoAppMember.ILogin.description:
Member login credentials with session context metadata for authentication.

This DTO is used when authenticating an existing member. The member provides their registered email address and password for credential verification against stored data.

Session context metadata (ip, href, referrer) is captured to establish an audit trail and enable security monitoring. Upon successful authentication, a new session record is created with these connection details for forensic analysis.

The password is transmitted securely over HTTPS and verified using bcrypt constant-time comparison to prevent timing-based attacks. This login endpoint is rate-limited to prevent brute force attacks.
ITodoAppMember.ILogin.x-autobe-specification:
Login request DTO for member authentication. Does not map to a single database table - it's a composite request type used across multiple tables during the login flow.

Data flow during authentication:
1. EMAIL: Used to lookup member record in todo_app_members.email column. Must match an existing active member.
2. PASSWORD: Plain text password verified against todo_app_members.password_hash using bcrypt constant-time comparison.
3. IP/HREF/REFERRER: Session context metadata captured from client request. Upon successful authentication, these populate todo_app_member_sessions table (ip, connection_href, connection_referrer columns).

Security: Password transmitted over HTTPS, verified with bcrypt. Session context used for audit trail and security monitoring. Rate limiting applied to prevent brute force attacks.

ITodoAppGuest.IRefresh.description:
Request DTO for refreshing a guest session's authentication tokens.

Contains the refresh token previously issued when the guest session was created. Upon successful validation, the server issues a new access token (15-minute validity) and a new refresh token (7-day validity), implementing token rotation for security.

The refresh token is validated by hashing and matching against stored hashes in the guest sessions table. If validation succeeds, the old refresh token is revoked and replaced with the new one to prevent replay attacks.

access.description:

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer

authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.

ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.

Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.
